title: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics (Standard) · Practice paper 2
subject: Mathematics (Standard)
label: Practice paper
instr: This question paper contains 38 questions. All questions are compulsory.
This question paper is divided into five sections: A, B, C, D and E.
In Section A, questions 1 to 18 are multiple choice questions (MCQs) and questions 19 and 20 are assertion-reason based questions of 1 mark each.
In Section B, questions 21 to 25 are very short answer (VSA) type questions carrying 2 marks each.
In Section C, questions 26 to 31 are short answer (SA) type questions carrying 3 marks each.
In Section D, questions 32 to 35 are long answer (LA) type questions carrying 5 marks each.
In Section E, questions 36 to 38 are case study based questions carrying 4 marks each. Each has three sub-parts (i), (ii) and (iii) of 1, 1 and 2 marks respectively.
There is no overall choice. Internal choices of the board paper are not included: each question has one version.
Draw neat and clean figures wherever required. Take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$ wherever required, if not stated.
Use of calculators is not allowed.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $p = 2^3 \times 3^2 \times 5$ and $q = 2^2 \times 3^3 \times 7$, then LCM$(p, q)$ is:
questions.sol: LCM = product of the highest powers of all prime factors $= 2^3 \times 3^3 \times 5 \times 7 = 7560$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the zeroes of the polynomial $x^2 - 5x + 6$, then the value of $\frac{1}{\alpha} + \frac{1}{\beta}$ is:
questions.sol: $\alpha + \beta = 5$, $\alpha\beta = 6$. $\frac{1}{\alpha} + \frac{1}{\beta} = \frac{\alpha + \beta}{\alpha\beta} = \frac{5}{6}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The pair of linear equations $3x - 2y = 5$ and $6x - 4y = 7$ has:
questions.sol: $\frac{3}{6} = \frac{-2}{-4} = \frac{1}{2}$ but $\frac{5}{7} \neq \frac{1}{2}$. The lines are parallel, so there is no solution.

questions.text: If $2k + 1$, 13 and $5k - 3$ are three consecutive terms of an A.P., then the value of $k$ is:
questions.sol: For consecutive terms of an A.P., $2 \times 13 = (2k + 1) + (5k - 3) \Rightarrow 26 = 7k - 2 \Rightarrow k = 4$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: PA and PB are tangents drawn from an external point P to a circle with centre O. If $\angle APB = 70^\circ$, then $\angle AOB$ is:
questions.sol: $\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^\circ$. In quadrilateral OAPB, $\angle AOB = 360^\circ - 90^\circ - 90^\circ - 70^\circ = 110^\circ$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the distance between the points $(4, k)$ and $(1, 0)$ is 5 units, then a possible value of $k$ is:
questions.sol: $(4 - 1)^2 + k^2 = 25 \Rightarrow k^2 = 16 \Rightarrow k = \pm 4$. Of the options, only 4 is possible.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\sqrt{3}\tan\theta = 1$, where $\theta$ is an acute angle, then the value of $\sin^2\theta - \cos^2\theta$ is:
questions.sol: $\tan\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \theta = 30^\circ$. $\sin^2 30^\circ - \cos^2 30^\circ = \frac{1}{4} - \frac{3}{4} = -\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 playing cards. The probability that it is a red face card is:
questions.sol: Red face cards: king, queen and jack of hearts and of diamonds, i.e. 6 cards. Probability $= \frac{6}{52} = \frac{3}{26}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The perimeter of a quadrant of a circle of radius 14 cm is:
questions.sol: Perimeter of a quadrant = arc + two radii $= \frac{1}{4} \times 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 14 + 2 \times 14 = 22 + 28 = 50$ cm.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A solid cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. A hemisphere of radius 7 cm is scooped out from one of its ends. The total surface area of the remaining solid is:
questions.sol: TSA = CSA of cylinder + area of the other base + inner surface of hemisphere $= 2\pi rh + \pi r^2 + 2\pi r^2 = 440 + 154 + 308 = 902\ \text{cm}^2$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: For a frequency distribution, $\sum f_i = 25$, $\sum f_i x_i = 50 + 5k$ and the mean is 6. The value of $k$ is:
questions.sol: Mean $= \frac{\sum f_i x_i}{\sum f_i} \Rightarrow 6 = \frac{50 + 5k}{25} \Rightarrow 150 = 50 + 5k \Rightarrow k = 20$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Which of the following cannot be the probability of an event?
questions.sol: The probability of an event lies between 0 and 1 (both included). 1.03 is greater than 1, so it cannot be a probability.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $(2, 3)$ is the mid-point of the line segment joining the points $(-3, 8)$ and $(a, -2)$, then the value of $a$ is:
questions.sol: $\frac{-3 + a}{2} = 2 \Rightarrow a = 7$. (Check: $\frac{8 + (-2)}{2} = 3$.)

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A hemispherical bowl has an inner radius of 10.5 cm. The volume of water it can hold is:
questions.sol: Volume $= \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 10.5 \times 10.5 \times 10.5 = 2425.5\ \text{cm}^3$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The length of the shadow of a vertical pole on level ground is $\sqrt{3}$ times the height of the pole. The angle of elevation of the Sun is:
questions.sol: $\tan\theta = \frac{h}{\sqrt{3}h} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \theta = 30^\circ$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Two coins are tossed together. The probability of getting at most one head is:
questions.sol: Outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT. At most one head: HT, TH, TT, i.e. 3 out of 4. Probability $= \frac{3}{4}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The point P(1, 2) divides the line segment joining A($-1$, 0) and B(5, 6) internally in the ratio 2 : 1.
Reason (R): The point dividing the line segment joining $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$ internally in the ratio $m : n$ is $\left(\frac{mx_2 + nx_1}{m + n}, \frac{my_2 + ny_1}{m + n}\right)$.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.sol: R is the section formula, so R is true. For ratio 2 : 1 the point is $\left(\frac{10 - 1}{3}, \frac{12 + 0}{3}\right) = (3, 4)$, not (1, 2). (P actually divides AB in the ratio 1 : 2.) So A is false.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The 10th term of the A.P. 5, 9, 13, ... is 41.
Reason (R): The common difference of an A.P. can be negative.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.sol: $a_{10} = 5 + 9 \times 4 = 41$, so A is true. R is also true (for example 10, 7, 4, ...), but it does not explain A.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Two buses leave a bus depot together at 6:00 a.m. One bus returns to the depot and leaves again every 40 minutes, and the other every 50 minutes. At what time will the two buses next leave the depot together?
questions.model:
$40 = 2^3 \times 5$ and $50 = 2 \times 5^2$
LCM(40, 50) $= 2^3 \times 5^2 = 200$ minutes = 3 hours 20 minutes
The buses will next leave together at 6:00 a.m. + 3 h 20 min = 9:20 a.m.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle PQR$, $\angle A = \angle P$, AB = 6 cm, AC = 8 cm, BC = 7 cm, PQ = 9 cm and PR = 12 cm. Show that $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQR$ and find QR.
questions.model:
$\frac{AB}{PQ} = \frac{6}{9} = \frac{2}{3}$ and $\frac{AC}{PR} = \frac{8}{12} = \frac{2}{3}$, and $\angle A = \angle P$.
So $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle PQR$ (SAS similarity criterion).
Hence $\frac{BC}{QR} = \frac{2}{3} \Rightarrow QR = \frac{3 \times 7}{2} = 10.5$ cm.

points.t: Ratios $\frac{AB}{PQ} = \frac{AC}{PR} = \frac{2}{3}$ with included angle equal, so similar by SAS

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A straight wheelchair ramp rises through a vertical height of 1.5 m and makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the level ground. Find the length of the ramp.
questions.model:
Let the length of the ramp be $L$ m. The ramp, the vertical rise and the ground form a right triangle.
$\sin 30^\circ = \frac{1.5}{L} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1.5}{L} \Rightarrow L = 3$ m
The ramp is 3 m long.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the area of the sector of a circle of radius 42 cm with central angle $60^\circ$. Also find the length of the arc of this sector.
questions.model:
Area of sector $= \frac{60}{360} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 42 \times 42 = \frac{1}{6} \times 5544 = 924\ \text{cm}^2$
Length of arc $= \frac{60}{360} \times 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 42 = \frac{1}{6} \times 264 = 44$ cm

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Given that $\sqrt{5}$ is an irrational number, prove that $7 - 2\sqrt{5}$ is an irrational number.
questions.model:
Let us assume that $7 - 2\sqrt{5}$ is rational. Then $7 - 2\sqrt{5} = \frac{a}{b}$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers and $b \neq 0$.
$\Rightarrow 2\sqrt{5} = 7 - \frac{a}{b} \Rightarrow \sqrt{5} = \frac{7b - a}{2b}$
Since $a$ and $b$ are integers, $\frac{7b - a}{2b}$ is rational, so $\sqrt{5}$ is rational.
This contradicts the given fact that $\sqrt{5}$ is irrational.
Hence our assumption is wrong, and $7 - 2\sqrt{5}$ is irrational.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: At a fruit shop, 5 kg of apples and 3 dozen bananas cost ₹680, while 3 kg of apples and 4 dozen bananas cost ₹540. Find the cost of 1 kg of apples and of 1 dozen bananas.
questions.model:
Let the cost of 1 kg of apples be ₹$x$ and of 1 dozen bananas be ₹$y$.
$5x + 3y = 680$ ...(1)
$3x + 4y = 540$ ...(2)
(1) $\times 4$: $20x + 12y = 2720$; (2) $\times 3$: $9x + 12y = 1620$
Subtracting: $11x = 1100 \Rightarrow x = 100$
From (1): $500 + 3y = 680 \Rightarrow y = 60$
1 kg of apples costs ₹100 and 1 dozen bananas cost ₹60.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the zeroes of the polynomial $x^2 - 6x + k$ such that $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = 20$, find the value of $k$. Hence find the zeroes of the polynomial.
questions.model:
$\alpha + \beta = 6$ and $\alpha\beta = k$
$\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta \Rightarrow 20 = 36 - 2k \Rightarrow k = 8$
The polynomial is $x^2 - 6x + 8 = (x - 2)(x - 4)$, so its zeroes are 2 and 4.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: S is a point on the side QR of $\triangle PQR$ such that $\angle PSR = \angle QPR$. If QR = 16 cm and SR = 9 cm, prove that $\triangle RSP \sim \triangle RPQ$ and find the length of PR.
questions.model:
In $\triangle RSP$ and $\triangle RPQ$:
$\angle PSR = \angle QPR$ (given)
$\angle SRP = \angle PRQ$ (common angle R)
So $\triangle RSP \sim \triangle RPQ$ (AA similarity criterion).
Hence $\frac{RS}{RP} = \frac{RP}{RQ} \Rightarrow RP^2 = RS \times RQ = 9 \times 16 = 144 \Rightarrow PR = 12$ cm.

points.t: Two pairs of equal angles stated, so $\triangle RSP \sim \triangle RPQ$ by AA

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The points A($-2$, 1), B($a$, 0), C(4, $b$) and D(1, 2) are the vertices of a parallelogram ABCD, taken in order. Find the values of $a$ and $b$.
questions.model:
The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so the mid-point of AC = the mid-point of BD.
Mid-point of AC $= \left(\frac{-2 + 4}{2}, \frac{1 + b}{2}\right) = \left(1, \frac{1 + b}{2}\right)$
Mid-point of BD $= \left(\frac{a + 1}{2}, \frac{0 + 2}{2}\right) = \left(\frac{a + 1}{2}, 1\right)$
$\frac{a + 1}{2} = 1 \Rightarrow a = 1$; $\frac{1 + b}{2} = 1 \Rightarrow b = 1$

points.t: Using mid-point of AC = mid-point of BD, with both mid-points written

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The length of a rectangular field is 1 m more than twice its breadth, and the area of the field is $528\ \text{m}^2$. Find the length and breadth of the field. Also find the cost of fencing the field at the rate of ₹50 per metre.
questions.model:
Let the breadth be $x$ m. Then the length is $(2x + 1)$ m.
$x(2x + 1) = 528 \Rightarrow 2x^2 + x - 528 = 0$
$\Rightarrow 2x^2 - 32x + 33x - 528 = 0 \Rightarrow 2x(x - 16) + 33(x - 16) = 0 \Rightarrow (x - 16)(2x + 33) = 0$
$\Rightarrow x = 16$ or $x = -\frac{33}{2}$. Breadth cannot be negative, so $x = 16$.
Breadth = 16 m, length $= 2 \times 16 + 1 = 33$ m.
Perimeter $= 2(33 + 16) = 98$ m; cost of fencing $= 98 \times 50 =$ ₹4900.

points.t: Rejecting the negative value: breadth 16 m and length 33 m

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
Prove that the lengths of the tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.
Using this result, solve the following: A circle is inscribed in $\triangle ABC$, touching the sides AB, BC and CA at P, Q and R respectively. If AB = 10 cm, BC = 12 cm and CA = 8 cm, find the lengths of AP, BQ and CR.
questions.model:
Given: PA and PB are tangents from an external point P to a circle with centre O, touching it at A and B.
To prove: PA = PB.
Construction: Join OA, OB and OP.
Proof: $\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^\circ$ (radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact).
In right triangles OAP and OBP: OA = OB (radii) and OP = OP (common).
So $\triangle OAP \cong \triangle OBP$ (RHS congruence), and hence PA = PB (CPCT).

Application: Let AP = AR = $x$, BP = BQ = $y$ and CQ = CR = $z$ (tangents from the same external point).
$x + y = 10$, $y + z = 12$, $z + x = 8$. Adding: $2(x + y + z) = 30 \Rightarrow x + y + z = 15$.
$x = 15 - 12 = 3$, $y = 15 - 8 = 7$, $z = 15 - 10 = 5$.
AP = 3 cm, BQ = 7 cm, CR = 5 cm.

points.t: Correct figure, given, to prove and construction
$\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^\circ$, OA = OB, OP common
Equations $x + y = 10$, $y + z = 12$, $z + x = 8$ using equal tangents
AP = 3 cm, BQ = 7 cm, CR = 5 cm

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A solid metal piece is in the shape of a cylinder with a hemisphere attached at each end. The diameter of the piece is 21 cm and its total length is 45 cm. Find the volume of the metal and the total surface area of the piece. Also find the cost of polishing its surface at the rate of ₹10 per $100\ \text{cm}^2$.
questions.model:
Radius $r = 10.5$ cm; length of the cylindrical part $h = 45 - 2 \times 10.5 = 24$ cm.
Volume of cylinder $= \pi r^2 h = \frac{22}{7} \times 10.5 \times 10.5 \times 24 = 8316\ \text{cm}^3$
Volume of two hemispheres $= \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3} \times \frac{22}{7} \times 10.5 \times 10.5 \times 10.5 = 4851\ \text{cm}^3$
Volume of metal $= 8316 + 4851 = 13167\ \text{cm}^3$
CSA of cylinder $= 2\pi rh = 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 10.5 \times 24 = 1584\ \text{cm}^2$
CSA of two hemispheres $= 4\pi r^2 = 4 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 10.5 \times 10.5 = 1386\ \text{cm}^2$
Total surface area $= 1584 + 1386 = 2970\ \text{cm}^2$
Cost of polishing $= \frac{2970}{100} \times 10 =$ ₹297

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A man standing on one bank of a river observes that the angle of elevation of the top of a tree standing on the opposite bank, exactly across, is $60^\circ$. When he walks 40 m straight back from the bank, directly away from the tree, the angle of elevation becomes $30^\circ$. Find the height of the tree and the width of the river.
questions.model:
Let AB be the tree of height $h$ m, C the first position of the man on the bank and D the second position, with B, C, D in a line. Let BC (width of the river) = $x$ m, so BD $= (x + 40)$ m.
In right $\triangle ABC$: $\tan 60^\circ = \frac{h}{x} \Rightarrow h = \sqrt{3}x$ ...(1)
In right $\triangle ABD$: $\tan 30^\circ = \frac{h}{x + 40} \Rightarrow h = \frac{x + 40}{\sqrt{3}}$ ...(2)
From (1) and (2): $\sqrt{3}x = \frac{x + 40}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow 3x = x + 40 \Rightarrow x = 20$
$h = 20\sqrt{3}$ m
Height of the tree $= 20\sqrt{3}$ m; width of the river = 20 m.

Based on the above information, answer the following questions:

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
On a sunny morning, Kabir measured that a vertical pole 6 m high casts a shadow 4 m long on level ground. At the same time, a nearby vertical tower casts a shadow 28 m long. The Sun's rays are parallel, so the pole with its shadow and the tower with its shadow form two right triangles.
Based on the above information, answer the following questions:

parts.q: (i) Name the similarity criterion by which the two triangles are similar.
parts.model: Each triangle has a right angle at the foot of the object, and the angle of elevation of the Sun at the tip of each shadow is the same (parallel rays). So the triangles are similar by the AA criterion.

parts.q: (ii) Find the height of the tower.
parts.model: $\frac{\text{height of tower}}{28} = \frac{6}{4} \Rightarrow$ height of tower $= 42$ m.

parts.q: (iii) At the same time, a boy 1.5 m tall stands on the line of the tower's shadow so that the tip of his shadow falls exactly at the tip of the tower's shadow. Find the length of the boy's shadow and his distance from the foot of the tower.
parts.model:
Boy's shadow: $\frac{1.5}{s} = \frac{6}{4} \Rightarrow s = 1$ m.
Distance of the boy from the foot of the tower $= 28 - 1 = 27$ m.

points.t: Length of the boy's shadow = 1 m
Distance from the foot of the tower = 27 m

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
At a school fair, a game stall has a bag containing 60 tokens, each of which is red, blue or green. A player draws one token at random. The probability of drawing a red token is $\frac{1}{4}$ and the probability of drawing a blue token is $\frac{1}{3}$.
Based on the above information, answer the following questions:

parts.q: (i) How many red tokens are there in the bag?
(ii) Find the probability of drawing a green token.
(iii) The stall keeper adds 5 more blue tokens to the bag. Find the probability of drawing a blue token now.
parts.model:
Blue tokens at first $= \frac{1}{3} \times 60 = 20$. After adding 5: blue tokens = 25 and total tokens = 65.
P(blue) $= \frac{25}{65} = \frac{5}{13}$.

points.t: Blue tokens = 25 and total = 65 after adding
